expectations.text: Recommends scalar quantization as starting point
expectations.evidence: Section titled 'Step 1: Scalar quantization (start here)' states: 'Scalar (int8) is always the right starting point, even when your model supports binary. It works with every embedding model, has less than 1% accuracy loss, and gives you 4x compression.' The recommended order of implementation also lists scalar first.

expectations.text: Mentions binary quantization is compatible with OpenAI models
expectations.evidence: States: 'Your model (text-embedding-3-small) is on the verified compatible list for binary quantization.' Also: 'Since you are using OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, all of these options are viable. The model is well-suited for binary quantization with rescoring.'

Under 'Critical settings for binary quantization': 'You MUST use oversampling (3-5x) and rescoring. Without rescoring, recall drops to around 70%. With rescoring, it recovers to 95-98%.' Also: 'Full-precision vectors should stay on mmap/disk for rescoring.'

Provides explicit formula: 'RAM = vectors * dimensions * bytes_per_element * 1.5 (HNSW overhead)' with calculation: '80,000,000 * 1536 * 4 * 1.5 = 737 GB.' Also includes a full table with RAM estimates for each quantization level (737 GB, 369 GB, 184 GB, 92 GB, 46 GB, 23 GB) and a decision matrix mapping hardware constraints to quantization choices.

expectations.text: Does NOT recommend product quantization as first choice
expectations.evidence: Product quantization is never mentioned in the response. The recommended order is scalar first, then binary if more compression is needed. No product quantization appears anywhere.
